# Purpose
This document provides an overview and instructions for Universal Ctags, a maintained implementation of `ctags`. Universal Ctags generates an index of language objects found in source files, facilitating easy navigation for text editors and other tools. The document outlines the project's history, features, and differences from its predecessor, Exuberant Ctags. It includes instructions for obtaining the latest builds for various operating systems and detailed steps for building and installing the software using Autotools. Additionally, it provides links to the primary documentation, including man pages and a hacking guide for developers. The document also addresses compatibility differences and security information related to CVE-2022-4515.
# Content Summary
The document provides an overview and technical details about Universal Ctags, a maintained implementation of the `ctags` tool. Universal Ctags generates an index of language objects found in source files, facilitating easy navigation for text editors and other tools. It continues the development of Exuberant Ctags, which introduced multi-language support and user-defined language parsing.

Key features of Universal Ctags include improved language support, an extended optlib for defining new language parsers, and an experimental interactive mode. The document provides instructions for obtaining the latest builds for different operating systems, including Windows, Unix-like systems, Mac, and Snap packages.

For building and installation, the document outlines steps using Autotools on GNU/Linux, OSX, or Windows 10 WSL, and provides links to additional documentation for specific platforms. The primary documentation for Universal Ctags is available in man pages, with additional resources in the Universal Ctags Hacking Guide.

The document highlights differences from Exuberant Ctags, such as changes in configuration file loading and stricter rules for kind letters and names. It also notes that Universal Ctags is not affected by CVE-2022-4515, as the issue was resolved in a 2016 commit. The document encourages contributions through pull requests.
